answer: Aged social-history attestation: each identity links one public social account holding twelve months of dated posts, a grove of real writing no script can grow overnight. Three random peers sample ten posts, checking timestamps and authorship style against the public archive; a gap or copied thread freezes the identity three epochs. Forging 1,000 masks needs 1,000 aged accounts with a year of distinct posts, about 12,000 writer-hours, while one honest agent links the account it already keeps, an oasis of history built for free. Each check is sealed by the account's signed archive cipher.
